questions.prompt: How many moles are in 20 g of calcium? (Ca = 40)
What is the formula of potassium carbonate? (K⁺, CO₃²⁻)
What is the molecular mass of nitric acid, HNO₃? (H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)
What mass of sodium hydroxide, NaOH, is 0.25 mol? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
Sulfur has the electron arrangement 2, 8, 6. Which ion does it form?
questions.explain: It gains 2 electrons to complete its octet.
Moles: H₂ 4 ÷ 2 = 2 mol; O₂ 16 ÷ 32 = 0.5 mol; H₂O 18 ÷ 18 = 1 mol; CO₂ 22 ÷ 44 = 0.5 mol. More moles means more molecules.

questions.prompt: Explain how you would find the number of atoms in a 5.6 g iron nail. (Fe = 56)
questions.modelAnswer: First convert mass to moles: n = m ÷ M = 5.6 ÷ 56 = 0.1 mol. Then multiply by the Avogadro constant: N = 0.1 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 6.022 × 10²² atoms.

questions.prompt: A student claims that 1 mole of sugar and 1 mole of salt must have the same mass because they are both 1 mole. Explain why they are wrong.
questions.modelAnswer: One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles (6.022 × 10²³), but the particles have different masses. A sucrose molecule (342 u) is much heavier than a sodium chloride formula unit (58.5 u), so 1 mol of sugar has a mass of 342 g while 1 mol of salt has a mass of 58.5 g.
rubric: A mole is a number of particles, not a mass
Particles of different substances have different masses
